best_for: Teachers, students and musicians who want to learn coding by making music, or to perform live by editing code on stage.

points.title: You play it by typing code
points.text: Sonic Pi is an instrument driven by short Ruby-style programs. A `live_loop` repeats while you edit it, so changes are heard on the next pass, which is how people perform with it.

points.title: A tutorial is built in
points.text: The help pane holds a 13-chapter tutorial plus lists of every synth, sample, effect and function. It was designed for school computing and music lessons.

points.title: Free, MIT, funded by fans
points.text: It is free and open source under the MIT license, made by over 200 contributors since 2012. The project asks for Patreon support rather than charging.

points.title: Desktop app over the web version
points.text: A browser version needs no install but does not work offline and has no OSC. The desktop app adds well-timed MIDI and OSC, low-latency audio through pro interfaces, Ableton Link and multichannel output. The Record button saves your set as a WAV file.

points.title: Requirements
points.text: Windows needs Windows 10 or 11, with x64 and Arm64 installers that install for the whole machine. The Mac builds, for Intel and Apple silicon, need macOS 13 Ventura or later; older Macs need an earlier release.

points.title: Linux: AppImage is the official route
points.text: The project publishes AppImage builds, including Arm64 for Raspberry Pi. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified.

points.title: Versions kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 19 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
